mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior 3 months indicates strengthening economic activity, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rising over 3 months does not yield positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% for at least 3 consecutive months, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy environment that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in inflation (CPIAUCSL) over the prior 3 months indicates a 'Goldilocks' economy with strong growth and cooling prices, which typically results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of PAYEMS rising and CPIAUCSL falling does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5.0% year-over-year), a decline in the federal funds rate signals an aggressive monetary easing that reduces real interest rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%), a decline in FEDFUNDS does not yield positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential housing starts (HOUST) over the prior 3 months indicates strong consumer confidence and construction activity, which typically leads to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST rising over 3 months does not correlate with positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% for at least 3 consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to wage pressures and inflation, causing the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in GDP growth (GDPC1) and residential housing starts (HOUST) over the prior 3 months indicates robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in GDPC1 and HOUST does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior 6 months indicates a strengthening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rising over 6 months does not correlate with positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases.
